mcat_description.short: Bamboo Huts are prefabricated or custom-built structures made primarily from treated bamboo poles and bamboo-based panels, sold as complete assembled units or in modular/prefab form for residential, hospitality, and eco-tourism applications.
mcat_description.long: Bamboo Huts are complete structural enclosures constructed using treated bamboo culms, bamboo panels, thatch or wooden roofing, and bamboo or FRP flooring, designed for deployment as standalone habitable or semi-habitable spaces. In the Indian B2B market, they are predominantly supplied as prefabricated or modular units to resorts, eco-tourism operators, restaurants, and farmhouse developers seeking a natural, sustainable aesthetic. Structural bamboo used in these huts is governed by BIS standards IS 15912:2018 (Structural Design Using Bamboo — Code of Practice) and IS 6874 (Method of Tests for Round Bamboos), with preservation requirements under IS 9096. Sizes are typically custom-quoted in square feet, with common footprints ranging from 10×10 ft to 20×15 ft, and lifespan varies from 5–25 years depending on bamboo treatment quality and maintenance regime.

market_context: In the Indian market, bamboo huts and bamboo houses are a well-established segment within prefabricated and eco-construction, with demand concentrated in hospitality (resorts, restaurants, eco-tourism camps) and residential applications in bamboo-rich states such as Assam, West Bengal, Odisha, and the Northeast. Structural bamboo construction in India is governed by BIS IS 15912:2018 (Structural Design Using Bamboo — Code of Practice, First Revision) and IS 6874 (Method of Tests for Round Bamboos), with bamboo preservation requirements under IS 9096:2006. The National Building Code of India (Section 3B: Timber and Bamboo) also covers bamboo as a structural material. Bamboo is recognised as a green building material and is noted for earthquake-resistant properties when used as a structural frame. Key manufacturing hubs include Delhi-NCR (Gurugram, Ghaziabad, New Delhi), Hyderabad, Pondicherry, Assam (Bongaigaon), and Pune. Sellers typically offer modular/prefab units quoted per sq ft, with custom sizing as the norm; common footprints are 10×10 ft to 20×15 ft. The dominant commercial form is a prefabricated or modular bamboo hut supplied to hospitality operators, with lifespan claims ranging from 5–25 years depending on treatment quality. Bamboo treatment (chemical preservation against fungi and insects) is a critical quality differentiator, as untreated bamboo has a natural durability of only 1–3 years. Regional buyer vocabulary includes 'baans ka ghar', 'baas ki jhopdi' (Hindi), and 'kudisai veedu' (Tamil). The category sits within the broader prefabricated structures market alongside bamboo gazebos and prefabricated huts.
